phrases.text: So welcome back again.
Time for one more problem.
Now in this problem,
we are given that a car covers two equal distances.
The first part is covered at forty kilometers per hour.
The second part is covered at sixty kilometers per hour.
The question is asking us to find the average speed for the whole journey.
Since both distances are equal,
let each distance be x kilometers.
Now we know the formula.
Time is equal to distance divided by speed.
So time taken to cover the first part is the distance covered in the first part,
which is
x, divided by the speed in the first part,
which is forty.
That is x by forty hours.
Similarly,
time taken to cover the second part is the distance covered in the second part, which is
x divided by the speed in the second part, which is sixty.
That is x by sixty hours.
Therefore, total time is x by forty plus x by sixty,
which simplifies to x by twenty-four hours.
The total distance is x plus x.
That is two x kilometers.
Now we know the average speed formula.
Average speed is equal to total distance divided by total time.
Putting the values,
average speed is equal to two x divided by x by twenty-four.
The x gets canceled and we are left with two into twenty-four, which is forty-eight kilometers per hour. So the average speed for the whole journey is forty-eight kilometers per hour.
Hence, the correct answer is option D.
